title: Alastair Graham
text:
Geographer for hire: looking to help the planet
I get stuff done.
I am a freelance physical geographer with a strong record of delivering practical, high-quality work. My background as an environmental technologist spans a range of applied and academic settings, giving me a broad and adaptable skill set. This ranges from technical computing, to scientific methods, to fieldwork, to teaching and training, to strategic thinking, and much more.
I love to learn, and as such I bring experience from both commercial and research environments. My approach is analytical, principled and pragmatic, with a focus on realistic solutions to complex environmental challenges. I am trusted to support and deliver complex projects to a high standard, on time and within budget. I place particular value on clear communication and enjoy explaining technical work to a wide range of audiences.
In addition to my professional work, I am an active podcaster as a co-host on the Geomob podcast (having previously created and hosted the Scene From Above podcast). I have also been a proactive longtime member of the OSGeo:UK committee (2017-2026) and currently volunteer for Green Tech South West.


Areas of Expertise and Interest
My career has focused on Earth observation for land applications. As such much of what drives me, and much of my experience, comes from wanting to understand landscape level patterns and changes driven by ecology, hydrology, geomorphology and more. Additionally, when something interests me I try to learn as much as I can about the subject: this has led me to understand quite a bit about home energy options and the technology available to help make your home comfortable.
A short list of my interests includes:

Land cover and habitats
Landscape processes and biogeography
Data and exploratory coding
Home energy

title: Additional information
text:
AI
AI as a term is being used as a catch all. Domain specific models such as those used for assessing ecology or remotely sensed data have a huge amount of utility in improving the speed and robustness of analysis. I am happy to work with these models and to use them in my work. However, I recognise the huge potential risks associated with big-tech’s large language models (LLMs). I would be happy to have a conversation about the use of LLMs to discuss the risks and benefits of their use. Working with specific, smaller, greener LLMs where appropriate is something I am interested in exploring.

title: What I do
text:
This page is a brief introduction to the types of work that I have done, what I like to do and what I am interested in. I am a big believer in allowing people to learn and push themselves, and I think the modern workplace often restricts people to a single specialism when they have so much more to offer. The generalist is often undervalued!
With that in mind, I often describe myself as an environmental technologist with a career in Earth observation.

Areas I can help with

Research and solutions around spatial and environmental problems
Project delivery and project management
Data manmagement and pre-processing of all sorts of data
Data processing using open source tools
Training and communication, including workshops, podcasts and videos
Strategic thinking for business development

Basically, if it’s interesting and I’m available then I’d love to collaborate with you and your team.


Specific skill areas

Remote sensing workflows and processing
Workflow architecture design
Open source GIS technical skills including spatial data science
Spatial strategy design and implementation
Environmental data analysis and interpretation
Scientific communication
Open standards advocacy
Home energy advice and advocacy



Future developments
I am currently interested in returning to undertaking some outdoor work. At the start of my career I undertook land cover and vegetation surveys as well as supporting hydrology fieldwork and would like to return to a bit more outdoor work. My interests are specifically in plants, vegetation and habitats but I am keen to garner new skills and experience where I can. If you would like an additional reliable person to help with your surveys then do get in touch.
My ideal future job would meet the description: Nature Recovery Innovation Manager. I would like to work with a team to help develop and implement innovative solutions to help nature recover. This could be through the use of technology, or through the development of new ways of working. If you are interested in working with me on this then please get in touch.
